Fulgĭnĭa , ae, f.,
I.a city of Umbria, between Perusia and Spoletium, now Foligno, Sil. 8, 462; Inscr. Orell. 2409.—
II. Deriv. Fulgĭnas , ātis, adj., of or belonging to Fulginia, Fulginian: municipium, Cic. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 768 P.: “in praefectura Fulginate,” id. ib. (Cic. vol. xi. p. 4 B. and K.). —In plur. subst.: Fulgĭnĭātes or Ful-gĭnātes , um, m., the inhabitants of Fulginia, Fulginians; form Fulginiates, Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 113; “form Fulginates,” Inscr. Don. 2 , no. 70 al.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
